page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 9 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong performance across multiple compute and memory workloads. The processor support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) drives strong results in specialized tasks, including a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 66,337.72 and a ray tracing score of 62,908.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 222.1 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 4,111.32 GB/sec for cached small blocks. In LLM inference tests, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 353.0 tokens/sec for a small 135M model, and strong prompt processing speeds of 246.51 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7i-flex.12xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for workloads that require high-frequency processing without the massive memory footprint of memory-optimized instances. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a streamlined option for CPU-bound tasks. It is highly suited for software compilation, batch processing, web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
